title: Throughput Safeguard Onboarding & Probation Lifecycle for Dedicated Reservations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement a structured probation and verification lifecycle for new Dedicated capacity reservations that guarantees committed throughput while protecting fleet stability and preventing runaway cost. This covers request intake, automated sizing checks, a staged canary/probation window with live throughput verification, autoscale policy alignment, billing holdback rules, and Console / API surfaces to expose probation state and telemetry to customers and SREs.
goals: 1) Ensure every committed reservation has an automated verification window that proves throughput guarantees before full billing and SLA take effect. 2) Provide engineers and customers clear rollback triggers and recovery playbooks if early usage destabilizes fleet. 3) Align autoscaling policies and fleet gating so canary traffic can be throttled without impacting other tenants.
acceptance_criteria:
- New reservation lifecycle includes a configurable probation window (default 72 hours).
- During probation the reservation is billed at a 50% holdback until verification passes.
- Telemetry dashboard shows 'probation' state, observed throughput, 95th latency, and resource contention signals.
- Automated verification job validates sustained throughput at >=90% of committed throughput for a rolling 1-hour window without causing cross-tenant SLO breaches.
- If verification fails twice, reservation auto-degrades to soft-commit (reduced throughput) and notifies customer with remediation steps.
- Admins can manually approve early graduation or extend probation via Console.
- All changes have audit logs recorded to the Private audit stream and included in the reservation history API.
proposal_summary: Introduce a 3-stage provisioning flow: Intake -> Canary (probation) -> Graduation. Intake runs automated sizing & pre-flight checks (quota, hardware fit, model compatibility). Canary assigns a limited fraction of capacity on a dedicated test pool with enhanced telemetry and strict autoscale ceilings. Graduation flips reservation to full capacity, releases billing holdback, and enables SLA window. New Console views and Reservation API flags expose state and controls.
key_work_items: Define probation defaults and knobs (duration, verification thresholds, billing holdback)
Implement reservation state machine in control plane (requested, preflight-passed, probation, graduated, degraded)
Autoscale policy alignment: enforce temporary ceiling and differentiated scaling rules during probation
Telemetry & dashboards: probation widget, probation history timeline, verification job logs
Billing & invoicing: implement holdback accounting and proration on graduation/failure
Runbook & customer messaging: canned email templates, Console banners, SRE incident playbooks
API contract: reservation state endpoints, admin approval endpoints, audit trail
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Longer probation increases time-to-value for customers but reduces fleet incidents.
- Billing holdbacks may frustrate customers who expect immediate full capacity; need clear comms and the option for manual waive.
- Dedicated test pool adds operational overhead and slightly reduces overall capacity available for production during probation spikes.
- Strict verification thresholds could cause false negatives for bursty workloads; mitigation includes rolling verification windows and sample-based tests.
ui_changes:
- Reservation detail page: show probation state, percent verified, next verification checkpoint, CTA to approve/extend.
- Onboarding modal with expected timelines and billing implications.
- Admin console: batch-approve probation graduations and view probation health matrix.
api_and_integration_notes:
- New fields on Reservation API: state (probation_start, probation_status, verified_percent), admin_actions (approve_early, extend_probation, force_degrade).
- Verification job posts results to /reservations/{id}/verification.
- Audit events published to private-audit topic: reservation.probation.started, .verified, .failed, .graduated, .degraded.
telemetry_requirements:
- Per-reservation metrics: observed_tput_rps, observed_tput_tokens, p95_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit_rate, cpu_utilization_gpu, queue_depth.
- Cross-tenant signals: fleet_backpressure_events, preemption_count, node_utilization_95.
- Alerting: probation_violation if observed throughput < threshold for 3 consecutive verification windows.
- Dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/dedicated/reservations/probation (placeholder)
notes: PM sync with Eng on 2026-02-20: agreed to enforce verification at 90% sustained throughput but allow looser thresholds for workloads with high variance using a customer-provided 'expected-variance' flag. Eng asked for an initial implementation focusing on N models and C instance types to reduce rollout scope.
